name: Rabindranath Tagore
summary: Tagore, a Bengali poet and educator, opposed British rule over India while rejecting nation-worship, which he called the organized selfishness of a people and a threat to humanity. He held that human relations rest on co-operation and spiritual unity rather than competition and power, favoured village self-help and education through Santiniketan and Sriniketan, and criticized Gandhi's charkha campaign as a blind faith. His recorded positions are mostly about nationalism, empire, race and caste, and education.

notes: Tagore had no office, so there is little record; positions come from his lectures and essays. Searched: nationalism, war and arms, empire and tutelage, race and caste, religion, education, economy and trade, cooperatives and village self-government, Gandhi's charkha and non-cooperation, Soviet Russia (Letters from Russia and Crisis in Civilization read only through secondary quotation), women, technology, ecology. Government, liberty, and most economy statements have no stated position found. Hindu-Muslim and women's questions rest only on a secondary account. Date: positions are mature (1917-1941).
